## MI5 Espionage Alert on China General Technology Research Institute


In the UK, MI5 issued a warning about the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI). According to[The News](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1418237-mi5-issues-rare-warning-over-chinese-institute-recruiting-uk-academics) , MI5 identified CGTRI as having obfuscated links to China's Ministry of State Security, and more than 100 UK academic institutions have engaged with it on secretly funded projects, with academics recruited to work on AI research and surveillance technology.


> "This alert exposes attempts by Chinese intelligence to covertly benefit from the expertise and research of our academics, undermining our national security, and that of our allies." UK Security Minister Dan Jarvis, as reported by The News


Jarvis added that he had written to all university Vice-Chancellors directing them to ensure staff end arrangements with the organization, per[The News](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1418237-mi5-issues-rare-warning-over-chinese-institute-recruiting-uk-academics) .


## Newsom Signs California AI Worker Protection Laws


On the regulatory front, California Governor Gavin Newsom signed several AI laws on Wednesday. As reported by[Click2Houston](https://www.click2houston.com/news/politics/2026/09/30/california-gov-gavin-newsom-signs-laws-to-protect-workers-from-ai-risks/) , the laws ban employers from using AI to predict workers' emotional states through biometric data, require written notice when AI is responsible for mass layoffs, and prevent employers from using AI as the sole basis for firing a worker.


"AI should expand opportunity, not come at the expense of workers and families," Newsom said, according to[Click2Houston](https://www.click2houston.com/news/politics/2026/09/30/california-gov-gavin-newsom-signs-laws-to-protect-workers-from-ai-risks/) . The report added that he criticized the federal government's lack of comprehensive AI regulation and left open the possibility of a special legislative session on further AI concerns.


## What It Means for Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft


The headlines matter for US-listed companies tied to the leading AI labs. According to[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/23/alphabet-vs-amazon-which-anthropic-backer-will-ben/) ,[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) holds an estimated 15% to 20% stake in Anthropic and[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) holds 10% to 15%, with the[Anthropic IPO](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-ahead-ai-stocks-in-focus/) expected in the next few months at a valuation of around $2 trillion. The same analysis noted that[Microsoft (MSFT)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/msft/) is closely tied to OpenAI.


The Motley Fool also pointed to a related report that Anthropic plans to spend $518 billion on cloud and data centers, with more than $100 billion already promised to Amazon. Distillation disputes, espionage warnings and state rules do not change those figures directly, but they add to the list of risks investors weigh when pricing the AI build-out.
